messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 HIGH severity alert: KV cache cardinality spike (prefix="user_prompt_v2") detected in us-west-2. Heap of unique keys grew from ~4k to ~1.1M in 12m. Continuous-batcher queue length >2000, tail latency spike to 7s, error rate 28%. Dash: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv/kv-cardinality

michael_oncall: ack. paging eng-runtime and sres. I'm on call. starting triage — who can grab fast metrics and check tokenization pipeline?

lee_engineering: I can join. seeing same on the runtime dashboards, memory pressure on cache pods -> OOM risk. suspecting prefix churn from prompt key normalization. hitting /metrics now.

sara_sre: i've started a read-only snapshot of the cache and taken a sample of keys. running: `redis-cli -h kv-primary --scan --pattern 'user_prompt_v2:*' | wc -l` -> ~1,123,412 keys. TTL distribution shows a lot with TTL=0 (never expire) and many with tiny TTLs oscillating.

michael_oncall: initial mitigation options: 1) throttle continuous batching (disable or reduce window), 2) apply a short-term TTL to new keys, 3) route heavy customers to fallback model. Which is the quickest?

lee_engineering: quickest is toggle continuous batching off for the affected model route and set max_batch_tokens=1024 -> reduces the in-flight KV write rate. I'll prepare a patch to the route config. Also recommend a temporary global prefix-ttl=60s for new keys (non-destructive).

carla_support: heads-up — two paying customers (acct-123, acct-456) are already reporting elevated error rates in their apps. they're waiting on an ETA. I'll open an escalation with CS and attach the mitigation notes.

sara_sre: running a targeted purge script to remove low-value ephemeral keys from the sample (non-destructive, safe windowed deletes). snippet:```bash
# careful -- dry-run first
redis-cli -h kv-primary --scan --pattern 'user_prompt_v2:*' | while read k; do
  ttl=$(redis-cli -h kv-primary TTL "$k")
  if [ "$ttl" -lt 5 ]; then
    echo purge:$k
    # redis-cli -h kv-primary DEL "$k"
  fi
done
```

ops-bot: Customer impact summary automated: estimated failed/errored requests during incident window 09:17:30-10:03:45 UTC = 3,732; error spike concentrated on /v1/generate endpoints in host-us-west-2; 95th p99 latency up to 7.2s. Tags: billing:high-impact, region:us-west-2.

lee_engineering: deploying two quick changes now: 1) route change to disable continuous batching for model-id: redwood/rlm-large-v2 in us-west-2, 2) runtime config patch to set prefix-ttl=60 for user_prompt_v2 keys. Patch:```yaml
# rollout patch
routes:
  - id: route-userprompt-v2
    model: redwood/rlm-large-v2
    batching:
      continuous: false
      window_ms: 5
    kv:
      prefix_ttl_override:
        user_prompt_v2: 60
```

lee_engineering: applying patch with rolloutctl: `rolloutctl apply -f patch.yaml --region us-west-2 --reason 'kv-cardinality spike mitigation'`

michael_oncall: while that's rolling, can we create a fallback traffic rule? small-llm-v1 should handle about 30% traffic for affected customers to reduce load.

eng-ml-bot: note: small-llm-v1 has different tokenization pipeline (legacy tokenizer v1). must verify compatibility with prompt templates.

lee_engineering: good catch. we'll only route customers with known stable prompt templates. adding immediate match: customer_id in [acct-789, acct-999] to fallback.

sara_sre: patch applied (confirmed) and purge dry-run output shows ~480k candidates for TTL<5s; we'll proceed with a staged delete: 5k keys/minute window to avoid thundering. running staged purge now.

carla_support: I told acct-123 we have a mitigation in flight (re-route + throttles) and ETA ~20m for stabilization. they're asking if any data loss — confirmed no user-level data deleted, only ephemeral cache keys.

lee_engineering: rolling back a recent batch-config change that landed ~2h before spike (commit 9f8a7e2). It bumped continuous_batch_threshold from 8->2 (more aggressive). Command: `git revert --no-commit 9f8a7e2 && rolloutctl apply -f routes/route-userprompt-v2.yaml`

michael_oncall: any signs on root cause? we should try to be precise before postmortem.

lee_engineering: initial root-cause hypothesis: an ML infra change to the prompt template generator introduced variable whitespace+template markers which, combined with a tokenizer version mismatch earlier this week, caused the entropy-mapper to produce a much wider distribution of prefix token sequences. Two things happened together: a) tokenizer v2 changed how certain punctuation is tokenized, b) template drift added ephemeral metadata into prompts. That produced vastly more unique keys and many tiny-lived cache entries.

eng-ml-bot: ML note: tokenizer v2 rolled on canary 04:12 UTC, rollout to prod 05:30 UTC per deploy bot log. Template change #PR-412 merged at 06:09 UTC. Correlation window fits. Recommend stall further tokenizer rollouts until we have compatibility tests.

sara_sre: after the staged purge and route throttles, cache cardinality is down to ~18k keys for the prefix. 95th latency stabilized to ~320ms, error rate back to baseline.

ops-bot: update: affected customers list now: acct-123 (high), acct-456 (high), acct-789 (medium). Incident window: 2912343456 -> 2912345825 (as measured by APM traces). Estimated 3.7k failed/errored requests.

carla_support: opened customer incidents and created interim KB for CS: 'KV cache spike: what to tell customers' (link internal).

michael_oncall: handing off to maria_nextoncall for follow-up/off-hours monitoring. Maria — please own the cleanup checklist and postmortem write-up. Items: 1) reproduce locally with tokenizer v2 + template drift, 2) add unit/integration test to alert on prefix-cardinality regression, 3) add alerting for per-prefix cardinality growth > 5x in 10m, 4) schedule rollback window for tokenizer rollouts.

maria_nextoncall: ack, taking handoff. I'll run a deep-dive tomorrow morning, will coordinate with eng-ml to freeze tokenizer rollout until tests added.

lee_engineering: follow-up items I'll own: create normalization step in prefix key generation to strip template metadata and enforce a stable hashing function (SHA256 truncated) and add safe guard TTLs for new keys defaulting to 60s.

michael_oncall: great. final note: incident severity reduced to P2, we've documented immediate actions. please add PR numbers and ownership to the postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident marked: mitigated. Notifications: #oncall, #cs, #eng-ml. Postmortem template: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/template.

eng-ml-bot: assigned to eng-ml: tokenizer compatibility audit + unit tests.

carla_support: closing customer escalations for now, will re-open if they see new spikes.

maria_nextoncall: logging handoff notes: stabilized at 10:03:45 UTC, purge complete, rollback applied. I'll produce a drafts timeline and RCA by EOD tomorrow.
